data.situation:
The clinic corridor opened into a small public-health display. While waiting for her transport, Maya followed the dates along the wall. A historical panel concerned plague, a particular disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. Beside it, a separate map illustrated a flu epidemic. The labels gave her two different kinds of information: plague named a disease, while epidemic described an outbreak with more cases than expected in a population and period. At the next panel, a speaker explained the aim of programmes to immunise people against particular diseases. Maya read each caption before comparing the examples. A final note used eradicate for the goal of completely removing a disease worldwide. Maya crossed out a draft sentence that treated a local fall in cases as proof of eradication. The wall offered a sequence of questions—what causes the disease, how the outbreak is described, and what a programme aims to achieve—rather than a list of interchangeable names. The immune-response diagram
A pathogen is an organism or other infectious agent that can cause disease. In this simplified drawing, an antigen appears on the surface of the illustrated pathogen. An antibody is a protein involved in recognising and binding a particular antigen. The three labels describe different roles; an antigen is not itself another word for the whole pathogen. Vaccination can prepare an immune response against a particular disease, but protection is not an unconditional guarantee. The display describes the process, not a choice of treatment for an individual visitor. Maya: Could I label every fast-spreading disease plague?
Speaker: No. On the historical panel it names a particular disease. Read the organism named beneath it.
Maya: And if cases become rare here, has the disease been eradicated?
Speaker: That would not establish worldwide eradication. Keep the scale and the period clear.
Maya: Then I will leave the disease name beside the timeline and the programme goal beside the map.

readingBlocks.zh: 诊所走廊通向一个小型公共卫生展区。等车时，玛雅沿着墙上的日期阅读。一块历史展板讲鼠疫，这是由鼠疫耶尔森菌引起的一种特定疾病。旁边另一张地图示范流感的流行情况。这两个标签提供不同信息：plague给疾病命名，epidemic描述某一人群和时期病例超过通常预期的暴发。下一块展板前，讲解者说明针对特定疾病开展免疫接种项目的目的。玛雅先读每块展板的说明，再比较这些例子。最后一条说明用eradicate表达在全球彻底消除一种疾病的目标。玛雅划掉了草稿中把本地病例下降当作根除证明的一句。墙上串起几个问题——疾病由什么引起、怎样描述暴发、项目想实现什么——而不是列一组可以互换的名称。

The immune-response diagram
A pathogen is an organism or other infectious agent that can cause disease. In this simplified drawing, an antigen appears on the surface of the illustrated pathogen. An antibody is a protein involved in recognising and binding a particular antigen. The three labels describe different roles; an antigen is not itself another word for the whole pathogen. Vaccination can prepare an immune response against a particular disease, but protection is not an unconditional guarantee. The display describes the process, not a choice of treatment for an individual visitor.
readingBlocks.zh:
免疫反应示意图
pathogen指能够引起疾病的生物体或其他感染性因子。这个简化图中，antigen标在所画病原体的表面。antibody是参与识别并结合特定抗原的一种蛋白质。三个标签描述不同角色，antigen不是整个pathogen的另一个名称。接种疫苗可以为针对特定疾病的免疫反应作准备，但保护不是无条件保证。展板说明这一过程，不替某位访客选择治疗。

readingBlocks.en:
Maya: Could I label every fast-spreading disease plague?
Speaker: No. On the historical panel it names a particular disease. Read the organism named beneath it.
Maya: And if cases become rare here, has the disease been eradicated?
Speaker: That would not establish worldwide eradication. Keep the scale and the period clear.
Maya: Then I will leave the disease name beside the timeline and the programme goal beside the map.
readingBlocks.zh:
玛雅：能把每一种传播快的疾病都标成plague吗？
讲解者：不能。历史展板上它是一种特定疾病的名称，看一下下方写的病原生物。
玛雅：如果这里病例变少，疾病就被根除了吗？
讲解者：这不能确定全球根除。范围与时期要说清楚。
玛雅：那我把疾病名称留在时间线旁，项目目标放在地图旁。

glossary.note: 名词plague；本展板指鼠疫这一疾病。

externalEvidence.definition: a serious (sometimes fatal) infection of rodents caused by Yersinia pestis and accidentally transmitted to humans by the bite of a flea that has bitten an infected animal

externalEvidence.label: Cambridge Dictionary
externalEvidence.reviewFinding: Noun can name a severe disease more broadly, often bubonic plague; present medical display selects the named disease only.

glossary.zh: 流行；病例高于预期的疾病暴发
glossary.note: 可数名词 an epidemic of ... / a flu epidemic；关注给定人群和时期的病例超过通常预期，不是某一种病原体的名字。
glossary.example: A separate map illustrated a flu epidemic.
glossary.exampleZh: 另一张地图示范流感的流行情况。

externalEvidence.definition: a widespread outbreak of an infectious disease; many people are infected at the same time

glossary.example: The final note described the goal of eradicating a disease worldwide.
glossary.exampleZh: 最后一条说明描述了在全球根除一种疾病的目标。

externalEvidence.definition: destroy completely, as if down to the roots "root out corruption"

glossary.zh: 使获得免疫保护；实施免疫接种
glossary.note: 动词：immunise somebody against a disease；美式拼写immunize。
glossary.example: The speaker explained programmes to immunise people against particular diseases.
glossary.exampleZh: 讲解者说明了针对特定疾病开展免疫接种的项目。

externalEvidence.definition: perform vaccinations or produce immunity in by inoculation

glossary.zh: 病原体；可引起疾病的感染性因子
glossary.note: 可数名词pathogen；能引起疾病的病原体。
glossary.example: The diagram showed an antigen on the surface of the illustrated pathogen.
glossary.exampleZh: 图上在所画病原体表面标出了抗原。

externalEvidence.definition: any disease-producing agent (especially a virus or bacterium or other microorganism)

glossary.note: 可数名词antigen；本图标在病原体表面。
glossary.example: An antigen appears on the surface of the illustrated pathogen.
glossary.exampleZh: 所画病原体的表面标出一种抗原。

externalEvidence.definition: any substance (as a toxin or enzyme) that stimulates an immune response in the body (especially the production of antibodies)

glossary.note: 可数名词antibody；常用bind/recognise an antigen。
glossary.example: An antibody can bind a particular antigen.
glossary.exampleZh: 抗体可以结合特定抗原。

retrievalPrompts.function: Three labels on the health display
retrievalPrompts.cue: Explain to a visitor the difference between the named disease and the description of an outbreak on the display.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 给参观者解释展板中疾病名称和暴发描述的区别。
acceptableAnswers: Plague names a particular disease on this historical panel. An epidemic describes an outbreak with more cases than expected in a particular population and period. The flu map illustrates the second term.
retrievalPrompts.feedbackZh: plague 在这块展板里命名疾病；an epidemic 是可数名词，可用 a flu epidemic 或 an epidemic of 某病说明暴发。解释区别时，要同时交代疾病名称与病例发生规模这两个层面。
checks: 说明历史展板中的 plague 指鼠疫这一特定疾病，不是所有快速传播疾病的通称。
说明 epidemic 描述某人群、某时期病例超过通常预期的暴发。
不把两者当作同一层面的病名；可用流感地图说明暴发描述。
retrievalPrompts.answerRangeZh: 可用定义后举例，也可直接对照两块展板。需保留鼠疫为特定病名、流行描述给定人群和时期的超预期病例；不必照搬术语定义的全部措辞。

retrievalPrompts.function: Three labels on the health display
retrievalPrompts.cue: Write two sentences distinguishing an immunisation programme from the goal of worldwide eradication.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 为展览写两句项目说明，区分实施免疫接种和全球根除目标。
acceptableAnswers: The programme aims to immunise people against particular diseases. To eradicate a disease worldwide is a different goal; fewer local cases alone would not establish that it had been achieved.
retrievalPrompts.feedbackZh: immunise somebody against a disease 中 against 接要防护的疾病；eradicate 直接接被根除的疾病。两句可分别说明项目做什么与最终目标是什么，避免把接种活动写成根除已经实现。
checks: 说明项目针对特定疾病开展免疫接种，immunise 若使用则对象是人。
将 eradicate 的全球彻底消除目标与免疫接种项目区别开来。
保持题目要求的两句；若举本地病例减少的例子，不把它当作全球根除证明。
retrievalPrompts.answerRangeZh: 允许使用 immunize 的美式拼写，或换一种两句的对照结构。须保留针对特定疾病的接种与全球根除是不同目标；可补充本地病例减少不足以证明根除，不必照搬反例句。

retrievalPrompts.function: Three labels on the health display
retrievalPrompts.cue: Put the three labels back into the diagram and explain their different roles in full sentences.
retrievalPrompts.cueZh: 把三个标签放回图中的角色，用完整句子说清关系。
acceptableAnswers: In this diagram, an antigen is shown on the pathogen. An antibody can recognise and bind a particular antigen. The labels refer to the disease-causing agent, a recognised substance and an immune protein respectively.
retrievalPrompts.feedbackZh: 三个词在图中各自有角色，antibody 可作 recognise 或 bind 的主语，antigen 是相应对象。解释位置时用“本图中”限定简化示意，既能说清关系，也避免把标签当成彼此的同义词。
checks: 区分 pathogen 的致病感染性因子角色、antigen 的被识别物质角色和 antibody 的免疫蛋白角色。
把抗原在病原体表面的位置限定为本示意图，不扩大成所有抗原的固定位置。
用完整句子说明抗体识别并结合特定抗原，不能把作用方向倒置。
retrievalPrompts.answerRangeZh: 可以改变介绍三个角色的顺序，recognise 与 bind 可在一句或多句中表达。必须保留三者的区别及抗体与抗原的关系；不需补写图外的免疫过程或治疗建议。

transferPrompt.function: Three labels on the health display
transferPrompt.cue: Another community display says fewer local cases mean the disease is eradicated. Revise the statement to make its geographical scope clear.
transferPrompt.cueZh: 为另一个社区展览修改“本地减少病例说明疾病已根除”的说明，提出范围清楚的表达。
acceptableAnswers: Cases have fallen in this local area during the recorded period. This is different from eradicating the disease worldwide. The display should describe the local change and explain the wider goal separately.
transferPrompt.feedbackZh: eradicate 在此公共卫生语境表示彻底消除疾病，worldwide 决定目标范围。修正时先写清本地变化与全球目标的区别；若有时间记录，也可限定观察时期，不需要自行补出日期。
checks: 将已观察到的结果限定为本地区病例下降，可补充资料已给的记录时期。
明确区分局部下降与全球根除的范围。
改写不继续把本地病例下降当作疾病已经根除的证明。
transferPrompt.answerRangeZh: 可写成一条说明或几句解释；本地病例下降和全球目标尚不能由此证明是必保留的信息。可沿用题干的地区称呼，不必虚构数值、确切年份或全球进展。
